name: Caulk a bathtub neatly
blurb: A tidy silicone line stops water getting into the wall and instantly makes a bathroom look maintained. The preparation matters more than the piping.
gear: A caulking gun, a removal tool, masking tape
steps: Remove all the old caulk with a scraper — every trace, because silicone will not bond to old silicone.
Clean the joint with rubbing alcohol and let it dry completely. Any moisture or soap residue kills adhesion.
Fill the bath with water before caulking, so the joint is at its widest under load and the seal will not tear later.
Mask both sides of the joint with tape, leaving a consistent gap.
Cut the nozzle at 45 degrees to the width you want, and lay a continuous bead in one smooth pass, pushing rather than dragging.
Tool the bead with a wet finger or a shaping tool, then pull the tape off immediately while the silicone is wet, and leave it to cure 24 hours before use.
tips: Pulling the tape after the silicone skins over tears the edge. Remove it straight away.
A tiny nozzle opening gives you far more control than a wide one.
Empty the bath only after full curing.
proof: A continuous, even bead with crisp edges that stays watertight and mould-free for months.
